brief: Molavi says stocks were punched last week by AI-trade fear, oil and weak Nasdaq technicals, then round-tripped to a flat scoreboard; bruises and fatigue stayed. This week stocks were quieter but bonds weren't kinder: Meta's Muse refocused sentiment on AI positives and positioning turned 'much, much cleaner,' while Hormuz hope steepened the curve's short end without fixing what still feels 'unwindy' underneath. He frames the key question as how high yields (now above 5%) must go before asset allocation rotates out of equities or duration/multiples de-rate. He is looking through oil, hoping for lower, because falling crude eases long-end pressure; oil back to $80 would be a hidden tailwind making the Fed's hike path optional again, after pricing swung fast from 2-3 cuts to 3-4 hikes. Separately: Meta staged a 43% one-month Muse squeeze; Oracle's force majeure revived AI-credit doubts, with $18bn of Project Jupiter debt quoted 89-91 cents; sell-side pegs 2026 AI capex at $768bn against $255bn depreciation (2029: $1.2tn vs $581bn). The note also ranges, unresolved, over AI's inflation-to-deflation path, a 2027-28 public/private financing collision, food/water scarcity, AI TAM diffusion, and VC/unicorn scaling stats, closing: a further oil drop validates the bull case, otherwise this week was just the warmup.
